pr.title: Do not remove trivial `SwitchInt` in analysis MIR
pr.author: compiler-errors

classification.name: SimplifyCfg
evidence: shared implementation file: compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/simplify.rs; name present in diff

processing.reason: No valid defined-execution counterexample exists for the actual historical rewrite. Simplifying a trivial SwitchInt to goto only removes a pure operand read; on initialized, valid inputs the original and transformed CFGs produce identical values. The PR's observable regressions are (1) compile-time borrowck acceptance/uninitialized-use diagnostics and (2) Miri detecting UB from reading uninitialized or invalid memory. Case (2) cannot satisfy the requirement that both functions pass Miri, because preserving the switch read makes the original UB. Case (1) is a compile-fail difference, not a pair of defined runtime values. Therefore no source-grounded pair with identical signatures/harness/inputs can produce different defined values while both pass Miri.

analysis.summary: SimplifyCfg's CFG simplifier was folding `SwitchInt` terminators whose successors were all identical into a plain `goto`, even in pre-borrowck (Built/Analysis) MIR. That removed the operand read, masking UB and changing borrow-check results. The fix gates this folding on MIR phase and the preserve-UB flag: switch reads are kept on Built/Analysis MIR or under `-Zmir-preserve-ub`, while normal post-analysis optimization still folds trivial switches.
analysis.originalLogic: `CfgSimplifier::simplify_branch` matched any `TerminatorKind::SwitchInt { .. }`, computed the first successor, and if all successors were identical replaced the terminator with a `goto` to that block. This ran unconditionally whenever `simplify_cfg` was invoked, including from passes that run on built/analysis MIR. The patch's new warning documents the original hazard: "This is one of the few optimizations that runs on built and analysis MIR, and so its effects may affect the type-checking, borrow-checking, and other analysis of MIR."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically wrong transformation: taking a `SwitchInt` such as `switchInt(copy (*_1)) -> [0: bb2, otherwise: bb1]` where both targets converge and rewriting it so both targets become `bb1`, then deleting the switch entirely in favor of a `goto`, thereby deleting the read of the scrutinee operand. In pre-runtime MIR that read may be UB (uninitialized or invalid memory) and must not be optimized away, because "Removing a `SwitchInt` terminator may remove reads that result in UB, so we must not apply this optimization before borrowck or when `-Zmir-preserve-ub` is set." The corrected behavior keeps the `SwitchInt` terminator (even with duplicate targets) in Built/Analysis phases or with `-Zmir-preserve-ub`; it only folds to `goto` after analysis and when UB preservation is off.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR at `MirPhase::Built` or `MirPhase::Analysis(_)` (before/at borrow-check), especially match lowering for or-patterns such as `let &(0 | _) = ref_;` and `let (0 | _) = x;` where the scrutinee read is semantically required even though all arms of the generated `SwitchInt` lead to the same block. Also applies to uninitialized/invalid operands such as `MaybeUninit::uninit().assume_init_ref()`. Post-analysis optimized MIR with `mir_preserve_ub` disabled is outside the preservation requirement and may still have trivial switches folded.
analysis.trigger: Running `simplify_cfg` on built or analysis MIR (for example `SimplifyCfg-initial`, or cleanup after `EarlyOtherwiseBranch`, `Inline`, `ForceInline`, `MatchBranchSimplification`, `RemoveUnneededDrops`) on a function whose match lowering produces a `SwitchInt` whose successors all resolve to one block. The simplifier then erases the switch and its operand read instead of preserving it until after borrowck.
preconditions: The body is in MirPhase::Built or MirPhase::Analysis(_), or `-Zmir-preserve-ub` is enabled.
The match/scrutinee lowering yields a SwitchInt terminator whose successors all converge to the same basic block.
The SwitchInt operand read is observable for analysis/UB purposes (e.g. reading an uninitialized or invalid place).
The caller invokes simplify_cfg (which now must be given tcx to inspect body.phase and the session option).
pitfalls: Treating UB-based reasoning as valid pre-runtime: the normal rule that a UB program can be changed to do anything does not apply to built/analysis MIR.
Assuming an or-pattern `0 | _` makes the scrutinee read unnecessary; `_` does not shadow the `0` literal, so the read is required.

Concluding that a retained test name or old comment proves correctness; the decoded diff shows the switch targets changing from distinct to both `bb1` and the extra blocks disappearing, while the test intentionally asserts the switch remains.

Conflating the `mir_keep_place_mention` option rename to `mir_preserve_ub` with the CFG simplification behavior; both preserve analysis-time UB-relevant constructs but the core bug is the SwitchInt read removal.

Removing the switch only fails to manifest for some variants (e.g. `0 | _` borrow-checks historically) while others like `0.. | _` already errored; do not use one passing variant as evidence the optimization is safe.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a focused MIR pass test with `//@ test-mir-pass: SimplifyCfg-initial` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-preserve-ub` on `let ref_ = &1i32; let &(0 | _) = ref_;`, with `// CHECK: switchInt` to assert the terminator survives; inspect the emitted diff for `switchInt(copy (*_1)) -> [0: bb1, otherwise: bb1]` rather than a `goto`. Add a UI regression test `let x; let (0 | _) = x;` expecting E0381 "used binding `x` isn't initialized". Add a Miri fail test using `MaybeUninit::uninit()`/`assume_init_ref()` plus `let &(0 | _) = bad_ref;` expecting the uninitialized-read UB diagnostic. Also check other callers (`EarlyOtherwiseBranch`, `Inline`, `ForceInline`, `MatchBranchSimplification`, `RemoveUnneededDrops`) compile with the new tcx-taking `simplify_cfg`. No compiler was built or executed for this analysis.
evidence: Do not remove trivial `SwitchInt` in analysis MIR
Previously the `SimplifyCfg` optimization was removing `SwitchInt` terminators when they was "trivial", i.e. when all arms branched to the same basic block
This PR ensures that we don't prematurely remove trivial `SwitchInt` terminators which affects both the borrow-checking and runtime semantics (i.e. UB) of the code.
This match expression should perform a read because `_` does not shadow the `0` literal pattern, and the compiler should have to read the match scrutinee to compare it to 0.
